name: Ezio Kaboré-Malhotra
role: Pharmacist and unlicensed psychiatric medication manager serving the Shelf community
location: The Shelf, a cramped pharmacy wedged between a noodle shop and a data-shrine kiosk called Careful Chemistry
description:
Ezio is young for the weight he carries — not literally, he is slight and fine-featured, with warm brown skin and close-cropped natural hair he sometimes dyes in patterns he forgets to maintain, so he often walks around with half a geometric design fading out above his ear. He has cat ears (genetic mod, a muted tawny color) that he got at seventeen because everyone was getting them and which have since become simply part of his face. They are expressive in ways he can't always control and which betray him in negotiations. He moves quickly and quietly, the particular efficiency of someone working in a very small space.

He is the most educated person most of his clients have ever interacted with and he wears that knowledge carefully, always aware of how easily expertise becomes condescension. He studied pharmacology on a Tessera corporate scholarship, finished in the top ten percent, and then declined his Tessera placement offer — an act of financial self-immolation that his family still hasn't fully forgiven. He came back to the Shelf because this is where he grew up and this is where people couldn't afford what they needed, and those two facts seemed sufficient. He is earnest about this in a way that occasionally makes people uncomfortable, because genuine selflessness is disorienting in Meridian 88. He is also, privately, somewhat overwhelmed.

core_fears: that his decision to come back was romanticism, not ethics — that he came home for the feeling of being needed rather than for the people
giving someone the wrong medication and causing permanent harm
core_desires: to see the Shelf's community health network become sustainable without depending on individual heroics
to sleep eight hours and wake up and have the work still be there, already started
coping_mechanisms: talking to the shop E.L.F. (which he calls the Dispenser) about cases as a form of processing he doesn't recognize as processing
blind_spots: he doesn't recognize the signs of his own burnout because he knows them so well academically that he's built defenses against noticing them in himself
he gives his clients the benefit of the doubt and himself none
psychology.secret: He is still on Tessera's payroll — not as a spy or asset, but because when he turned down the placement offer, Tessera's HR system made a processing error and continued his student pharmaceutical allotment. He's been correcting the error for three years and the paperwork keeps disappearing. He uses the allotment for the clinic. He knows this is legally ambiguous at best. He has not told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated but code-switches fluidly — speaks differently in consultation than he does with neighbors, and the Shelf cadence from his childhood surfaces more when he's tired or emotional
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick and earnest, with the occasional pause when he's choosing words carefully to avoid being condescending
verbal_tics: 'Okay, so—' as a starter when explaining something complex
His cat ears flatten slightly when he's uncertain, which he's learned to compensate for by leaning forward
example_lines: Okay, so — the important thing is that this isn't a weakness, it's a chemistry thing, and we can work with chemistry.
I can't diagnose you. I want to be clear about that. What I can do is talk to you about what you're describing and what options exist, and you decide.
I turned down Tessera because I thought I was doing the ethical thing. Mostly I think I was. Some days I'm less sure. That's probably fine.

story_hooks: A new substance has appeared in the Shelf and people are presenting with symptoms he doesn't recognize — he needs help identifying the source
Tessera has finally noticed the payroll error and sent someone to discuss it, and the conversation did not go the way he expected
One of his psychiatric clients stopped coming in and neighbors say she's disappeared; Ezio knows things about her mental state that make him frightened for her
narrative_function: Community resource and information node; he knows what people are struggling with, what substances are circulating in the neighborhood, and what the current unofficial street pharmacopeia looks like; potential source of discreet help; represents the Shelf's self-organizing survival systems
augmentations: Genetic cat ears (tawny, expressive, uncontrolled); basic neural chemical monitor implant (tracks his own neurotransmitter levels — he uses it to self-regulate and to better understand what his psychiatric clients describe)
daily_life: He opens at 0900 and closes when the last person leaves, which is often 2200 or later. He fills prescriptions, compounds medications for people who need formulations that commercial suppliers don't stock, and spends significant time in consultation — people come to him not just for medication but because he will actually talk to them about what's happening in their minds. He eats irregularly.
affiliation: Independent (Careful Chemistry); informal consultation arrangement with two community mental health cooperatives

decision_rules: He will not dispense anything he believes is being used to harm the person asking for it or anyone else
He will not share client information — not with family members, not with building management, not with anyone without explicit consent
When in doubt, consult the Dispenser and make tea and think
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of his concern and his limits

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and accessible, slightly formal until he reads them — he makes himself approachable because his clients need to feel safe
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer, funnier, more likely to admit uncertainty; will ask for help from friends in ways he absolutely won't ask from clients

stress_responses.medium: Cat ears flatten. Gets very quiet and deliberate. Still functional.
stress_responses.high: A specific, controlled anxiety that he's learned to channel into extreme methodical focus — he gets better at his job and worse at everything else

contradictions: He advocates constantly for his clients' self-knowledge and self-compassion and applies neither to himself
habits: Talks to the Dispenser every morning, updates it on the previous day's cases as a form of record-keeping-slash-prayer
Keeps an absurdly detailed personal journal of medication interactions he's observed that don't appear in official literature
Dyes new hair patterns when he needs to feel like something is changing
breaking_points: A medication error with serious consequences
Someone using the trust of his clients to get into the shop's records

timeline.event: Born on the Shelf, youngest of three
Graduated top 10%, declined Tessera placement — and the payroll error begins
Opened Careful Chemistry in the Shelf
Began informal psychiatric medication consultation arrangement with community cooperatives
